title: Canonical presentation of an ind-constructible sheaf
statement:
Use the universe and small-site convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and a separated scheme $X$ of finite type over $k$, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and a finite intermediate extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\Lambda=\underline E$ or $\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$ be the condensed coefficient ring of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], and let $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ as in [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Work in $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X}$, the category of internal module objects of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Write $\mathcal C=\operatorname{Cons}(X,\Lambda)$ for its full subcategory of constructible sheaves [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and $\operatorname{IndCons}(X,\Lambda)$ for the full replete subcategory of objects isomorphic to small filtered colimits of objects of $\mathcal C$, as in [det-ind-heart-full-faithfulness]. Filtered diagrams and colimits have the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

Let $B\in\operatorname{IndCons}(X,\Lambda)$. Let $J(B)$ have objects $(C,c)$ with $C\in\mathcal C$ and $c:C\to B$, and morphisms $f:(C,c)\to(C',c')$ the maps $f:C\to C'$ satisfying $c'f=c$. Then $J(B)$ is essentially small and filtered, and its tautological cocone with legs $c:C\to B$ is a colimit in $\mathcal M$:
$$B\simeq\varinjlim_{(C,c)\in J(B)}C.$$
Here a colimit over an essentially small category is taken over a small skeleton. For every small filtered presentation $B\simeq\varinjlim_{i\in I}C_i$ with each $C_i\in\mathcal C$, the functor $F:I\to J(B)$ induced by the presentation cocone is final (cofinal).

proof.text: Finite type over the spectrum of the field k gives a locally Noetherian and quasi-compact X by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Apply [det-lem-coefficient-heart-small] for each of the two canonical condensed coefficient rings. The constructible full subcategory is essentially small, and its costructured-arrow category over B is essentially small by Mathlib CostructuredArrow.essentiallySmall, since ambient module morphisms lie in universe u+1.

Fix any small filtered constructible presentation of B. Clause (1) of [det-ind-heart-full-faithfulness] makes every constructible domain finitely presentable. Mathlib IsFinitelyPresentable.exists_hom_of_isColimit factors every constructible map to B through a presentation stage. IsFinitelyPresentable.exists_eq_of_isColimit makes two factorizations equal after two transition arrows; filtered equalization of those arrows gives one transition identifying the factorizations. Apply the filtered finality criterion of [lem-weil-pbc-initial-functor-cofiltered-criterion], in its dual form Functor.final_iff_of_isFiltered. This proves finality for every presentation.

The hypothesis that B lies in ObjectProperty.ind already supplies a small filtered constructible presentation, by [det-ind-heart-full-faithfulness] and the definition of IndCons. Its presentation functor is final by the preceding argument. Therefore J(B) is filtered by Mathlib IsFiltered.of_final. This proves the filteredness conclusion without needing constructible closure under direct sums or cokernels.

source.place: Filtered and Cofinality paragraphs; derive filteredness from the final presentation

proof.text: Whisker the canonical tautological cocone with that presentation functor. The whiskered cocone is isomorphic to the presentation cocone by the identity on B, since its legs are the specified presentation legs. Transfer its IsColimit proof along Functor.Final.isColimitWhiskerEquiv, using [lem-weil-pbc-initial-functor-cofiltered-criterion] and [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. This constructs the colimit proof directly for the tautological cocone and hence proves density at B, without assuming existence of another chosen colimit.

proof_origin.place: Essential smallness, Cofinality and Colimit paragraphs; filteredness follows from the final presentation
